title: P4 eraser even-odd pointInEraser leaves un-erased fill slivers where eraser stamp loops overlap (default drag corruption)
description:
DEFECT (task 1322, commit 12db52f, packages/core/src/engine/planar/eraser.ts:77-83 pointInEraser).

planarEraseShape classifies which faces/strokes fall under the eraser via pointInEraser(), which uses EVEN-ODD parity across all eraser stamp loops:
  for (const loop of eraserLoops) if (pointInPolygon(pt, loop)) inside = !inside;
The eraser region is the UNION of the stamp loops, not their symmetric difference. Any point covered by an EVEN number of loops (2, 4, ...) reads inside=false and is wrongly treated as NOT erased -> the fill/stroke there survives.

REACHABLE ON THE DEFAULT DRAG PATH, not just adversarial multi-stroke: buildEraserStamp() emits one disk per sample PLUS a bridging capsule between consecutive samples, and consecutive disk+capsule loops OVERLAP heavily. So an ordinary eraser drag self-overlaps and leaves slivers along its own path.

PROVEN (scratch tests, removed):
- pointInEraser unit: center of two crossing bands (x in [92,108], y in [92,108]) at (102,102): even-odd=false, union=true. Geometrically inside the eraser, reported NOT erased.
- single drag buildEraserStamp([{x:50,y:50},{x:70,y:50}], 12) -> 3 loops; scanning a 60x40 grid, 374 points are union-inside but even-odd-outside (cover=2). Example (50,40) cover=2.
- END-TO-END: planarEraseShape(120x120 BLUE fill, buildEraserStamp([{x:40,y:60},{x:80,y:60}],14), normal) leaves 5 SURVIVING filled faces whose interior points are inside the eraser sweep: (32.2,61.0),(59.3,59.5),... Expected: zero surviving fill inside the swept region.
- plus-shaped two-band erase of a 200x200 fill yields 5 filled faces (4 quadrants + 1 spurious survivor at center (102,102)) instead of 4.

IMPACT: dragging the eraser across a fill leaves visible specks/slivers of the original fill along the drag path (and at any stamp-loop overlap); area not fully removed. Faucet/single-click (single disk, no overlap) is unaffected; non-overlapping isolated bites are fine.

ROOT CAUSE: even-odd parity used where a UNION (winding/any-inside) test is required. pointInEraser should return true if pt is inside ANY loop (union), e.g. 'for (const loop) if (pointInPolygon(pt,loop)) return true;'. Same fix applies to the stroke-midpoint test (eraseStrokes) which calls pointInEraser. NOTE the kernel SPLIT geometry is correct (all stamp loops are inserted as edges and split fills curve-preservingly); only the post-hoc face/stroke CLASSIFICATION via even-odd is wrong.

VERIFIED-OK around it: corner bite, isolated island hole, single non-overlapping band, coincident-along-edge, near-zero sliver, curve preservation (CurvedEdge survives in DefineShape4 encode), modes (fills/lines/inside/selected), faucet. golden hash 9d09912df4727d0c unchanged; swf 1466/1466; planar suites 82/82. Existing planar-eraser.test.ts passes because its drags/bands avoid sampling the overlap zones.

FIX + regression test: replace even-odd with union in pointInEraser; add a planar-eraser.test.ts case asserting NO filled face's interior point lies inside the eraser sweep union after a multi-sample drag.
